title: DVT and PE: acute, chronic or history
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for leg swelling.

HPI: Pt is an 87-year-old male presenting for f/u of known deep vein thrombosis. Pt reports stable symptoms with no new calf pain or significant swelling noted today. He is currently on long-term anticoagulation therapy. He denies any shortness of breath or chest pain. He reports compliance with medications.

Medication List:
- Warfarin 5mg QD
- Lisinopril 10mg QD
- Atorvastatin 20mg QD

Vitals:
BP: 132/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Wt: 175 lbs

Recent Labs:
INR: 2.4
HbA1c: 6.8%
eGFR: 65

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or fatigue.
CV: No palpitations, orthopnea, or chest pain.
Resp: No cough or SOB.
MSK: No new calf pain or swelling.
GI: No abdominal pain or changes in bowel habits.
GU: No dysuria.
Skin: No rashes or lesions.

Social History: Retired. Lives with wife. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Exam:
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, regular rhythm, no murmurs.
Lungs: CTAB.
Extremities: Exam of lower extremities shows stable findings. Right lower extremity shows mild residual swelling. No erythema or warmth. Pedal pulses 2+ bilaterally.

Assessment:
1. Chronic DVT of the right femoral vein. Ultrasound confirms residual clot. Pt is stable on current anticoagulation.

Plan:
1. Continue long-term anticoagulation.
2. Monitor INR regularly.
3. Pt to call if new calf pain or swelling develops.
4. F/u in 3 months.

Electronically signed, M. Okafor, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Chronic DVT of the right femoral vein: I82.511 (HCC 267).

distractors.why: The DVT is documented as chronic.
Chronic DVT is a current condition, not history.
